exercise: Multinomial Naive Bayes with Bigram LM Sentiment Classification

marking_grid.criteria: Correct lowercase, punctuation removal, lemmatization, and insertion of <s> and </s> tokens for each training sentence.
Correct vocabulary of 10 unique tokens: ['</s>', '<s>', 'act', 'bad', 'good', 'hate', 'like', 'movie', 'play', 'real'] with |V| = 10.

marking_grid.item: Test Sentence 1 Prior & Bigram Probability Calculations
marking_grid.criteria: P(pos) = 0.5, P(neg) = 0.5. Detailed bigram product showing P(pos|s1) ≈ 0.000174 and P(neg|s1) ≈ 0.000027.
Correctly concludes Predicted Class = Positive because P(pos|s1) > P(neg|s1).

sample_submissions.text:
For test sentence 1 '<s> like act bad </s>':
P(pos) = 0.5, P(neg) = 0.5
Pos: P(like|<s>)=3/12, P(act|like)=2/12, P(bad|act)=1/12, P(</s>|bad)=1/10. Product = 0.5 * 0.25 * 0.1667 * 0.0833 * 0.1 = 1.736e-4
Neg: P(like|<s>)=1/12, P(act|like)=1/10, P(bad|act)=1/11, P(</s>|bad)=1/14. Product = 0.5 * 0.0833 * 0.1 * 0.0909 * 0.0714 = 2.705e-5
Since 1.736e-4 > 2.705e-5, sentiment is Positive.
sample_submissions.feedback: Flawless solution. Correct smoothing, exact prior probabilities, accurate bigram transition calculations, and justified decision.

sample_submissions.text: P(pos) is 0.5. I multiplied the words: like, act, bad. P(pos) comes out larger than P(neg), so predicted class is Positive.
sample_submissions.feedback: Correct final prediction (+1.0), but missing explicit Laplace smoothing fractions, omitted <s> and </s> boundary transitions (-2.0), and failed to show intermediate bigram probabilities (-1.0).
